answer: Reciprocated-non-kin k-core gating resists sybils: earning weight requires sitting in the honest-seeded k-core of the mutual-attestation graph, where each counted edge is reciprocated by a non-kin peer. A sybil ring can thread countless edges among its own quill of fakes, but honest nodes refuse to reciprocate into an unvetted cluster, so the ring never attaches through the narrow inlet of real edges — lacking k reciprocated non-kin links, the whole cluster stays below threshold.
